findings.title: Denial cache key omits identity type, so anonymous and renderer share denials
findings.body: `userPermDenialCacheKey` is built from `checkReq.UserUID`, the ID part of the subject, and does not include the identity type. `anonymous:0` and `render:0` both yield UserUID `0`, so they get the same denial key for the same namespace, action, name and folder. The denial lookup in `Check` runs before any identity-specific logic. If an anonymous check on `dashboards:read` for `dash1` is denied, the denial is cached for 30s. A renderer check for the same dashboard is then denied from the cache, although the renderer is granted read on all dashboards and folders. The result is renders that fail intermittently for up to the TTL. The key should include the identity type, or the resolved internal UID, as the permission cache keys do.

findings.title: Underscore-joined denial key is ambiguous for names and folders that contain underscores
findings.body: The key is `ns.perm_<user>_<action>_<name>_<parent>`, joined with `_`. Dashboard and folder UIDs commonly contain underscores, so different (name, folder) pairs can map to the same key. For example, name `a_b` with folder `c` and name `a` with folder `b_c` both produce `..._a_b_c`. A denial for one resource then wrongly denies the other for the TTL. The key also shares the `perm_<user>_<action>` prefix with the permission-map key, which holds a different value type. Use an unambiguous separator or a distinct prefix such as `perm_denied_`, and consider hashing or escaping the components.

findings.title: Every first-time denial for a distinct resource triggers a DB permission re-query
findings.body: When cached permissions do not allow the request, `Check` always falls through to `getIdentityPermissions`, which queries the DB. The only mitigation is the denial cache, which is keyed per (user, action, name, folder). A user without access to many resources, such as a UI or search path that checks many dashboards individually, therefore causes one permission query per distinct denied resource until each has its own denial entry. Singleflight only deduplicates concurrent calls. This weakens the cache and can amplify load on the SQL permission store, including for unauthorized or probing callers who vary the resource name. Consider rate-limiting the re-query, for example a per-user/action 'recently refreshed' marker, so that a fresh DB fetch is not repeated within a short window.

findings.title: Cached denials are not invalidated when permissions are refreshed
findings.body: A denial entry is written for 30s and consulted before the permission cache. If a user's permissions are refreshed from the DB between the denial and a later check, for example by a check or List on another resource, the permission cache can already grant the resource. The denial entry still takes precedence, so access stays denied until the denial TTL expires. The same applies if a permission is granted after an earlier check on a not-yet-existing resource. This partly defeats the goal of letting a creator access a just-created dashboard or folder. When `getUserPermissions` repopulates the permission cache, the denial entry for the checked resource should be dropped, or the allowed result should be authoritative.

findings.title: Denial-cache test is vacuous: it would pass without the denial short-circuit
findings.body: The test 'Should deny on explicit cache deny entry' comments that it allows access to prove the permission cache is not consulted. It sets the permCache value to `false` (`{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`), which does not grant anything. Without the denial-cache logic, `checkPermission` would see no grant and fall through to the empty fake store, so the result is still `Allowed=false`. The test therefore passes whether or not the denial cache works. It should set the scope to `true` and/or use a store that would grant access, so that only the denial entry can produce the deny.

findings.title: No test that a DB-derived denial is written to the denial cache; removed cache-hit case leaves dead test fields
findings.body: The new tests cover reading a pre-seeded denial entry. None checks that `Check` writes a denial entry after a DB-confirmed deny, which is the behaviour that protects the DB from repeated queries. None checks that an allowed result does not write one. Nothing covers the anonymous or renderer paths through the new cache-then-DB flow, or the case where the identity lookup fails. The 'permissions from cache' case was also deleted from `TestService_getUserPermissions`, so the `cacheHit` field is now always false there and effectively dead code.
